input: Outline a personal finance course for my blog

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The target audience (e.g. total beginners, young adults, parents, high earners) determines which topics to include, the depth of explanation, and the assumed baseline knowledge.
Personal finance is broad — knowing which topics are in or out (budgeting, investing, debt, retirement, taxes, etc.) shapes the entire course structure and length.
The number of modules or lessons the user wants sets the granularity of the outline and how much can realistically be covered.
The country or region affects which financial systems, tax rules, account types, and regulations are relevant to reference in the course.
The tone and teaching style (practical/actionable vs. conceptual/educational, serious vs. conversational) determines how the outline frames lessons and calls to action.
The delivery format (standalone blog posts, a gated email course, a free PDF, etc.) changes how lessons should be structured, linked, and sequenced.
Knowing the primary outcome the user wants readers to achieve (e.g. build a budget, get out of debt, start investing) ensures the course arc leads to a clear, measurable transformation.

gold.taskTitle: Outline a personal finance course for blog
gold.taskDescription: Create a structured course outline on personal finance topics to be published as a blog-based course.

questions.title: Who is the target reader for this course?
questions.description: Identify the intended audience — e.g. complete beginners, millennials paying off debt, new parents, or people approaching retirement — to calibrate depth and relevance.

questions.title: Which finance topics must the course cover?
questions.description: Determine which subjects are in scope (budgeting, saving, investing, debt, taxes, insurance, retirement, etc.) and which should be excluded to keep the course focused.

questions.title: How many modules or lessons do you want?
questions.description: Establish the desired course length — for example, a 5-module overview vs. a 20-lesson deep dive — so the outline can be sized appropriately.

questions.title: Which country's financial system should this reflect?
questions.description: Pinpoint the geographic context so the outline references relevant account types, tax rules, and regulations (e.g. US 401k/Roth, UK ISA, Canadian TFSA).

questions.title: What tone should the course have?
questions.description: Clarify the preferred style — e.g. friendly and conversational, authoritative and academic, or motivational and action-driven — to shape how each lesson is framed.

questions.title: How will the course be delivered on your blog?
questions.description: Determine the delivery format — a series of public blog posts, a gated email drip course, a downloadable PDF guide, or a mix — since this affects how lessons connect and are sequenced.

questions.title: What should readers be able to do after finishing?
questions.description: Define the key transformation or outcome — e.g. build their first budget, open an investment account, eliminate credit card debt — so the course arc leads to one clear result.
